Start by setting the foundation. Help the person understand that growth isn't about being perfect; it's about making continuous progress. Encourage a growth mindset, frame challenges as learning opportunities, and remind them that improvement is possible with effort.

先打基础。帮这个人理解：成长不是要完美，而是要持续进步。鼓励成长型心态，把挑战框定为学习机会，并提醒他们：只要努力，改进是可能的。

Help them self-assess. For this, go back to the expectations of their role and evaluate—What are they already doing well? Where are the gaps?—going point by point. Once their assessment is done, provide your feedback on where they are and also ask them to collect feedback from the rest of the team members to ensure their assessment is accurate.

帮他们做自评。为此，回到其岗位的期望，逐条评估——他们已经做得好的是什么？缺口在哪里？自评完成后，就其现状给出你的反馈，同时请他们向团队其他成员收集反馈，以确保自评准确。

Then define a shared goal: “How will we know we've made progress?” Break it down into smaller, actionable steps. These could be tasks, habits, or skills they need to build. For example, if the goal is to improve communication, a milestone might be taking over the communication on a new initiative that involves working with another team.

然后定义一个共同目标：“我们怎么知道自己取得了进展？”把它拆成更小、可执行的步骤。这些可以是任务、习惯、或他们需要培养的技能。例如，如果目标是改善沟通，一个里程碑可能是：在一个需要与另一团队协作的新举措上，主导沟通工作。

Set a loose timeline. Don't overengineer it, just enough to create momentum and accountability. Milestones might span a few weeks or a couple of months, depending on the nature of the issue. From there, talk about who can support them. This might be you, other senior team members, a mentor, or even external coaching. Let those people know so they can offer guidance and help reinforce the plan.

定一个宽松的时间线。不要过度设计，只要足以形成势头和责任即可。里程碑可能跨越几周或一两个月，视问题性质而定。然后，谈一谈谁能支持他们。这可能是你、其他资深成员、一位导师、甚至外部教练。让这些人知道，好提供指导并帮着强化计划。

Just remember: support doesn't mean taking over. At the end of the day, it's still their responsibility to own the plan and follow through, so make that clear. You can create space, give guidance, and offer feedback, but you can't do the work for them. Improvement takes personal commitment. That's something no one else can provide on their behalf.

只要记住：支持不等于接管。归根结底，为计划负责并贯彻到底，仍是他们自己的责任，所以要讲清楚。你可以创造空间、给予指导、提供反馈，但你不能替他们去做。改进需要个人的投入。这是任何人都无法代劳的。

Also, look for stretch opportunities: are there projects or responsibilities that would help this person practice the skill they need to grow? Are there books, courses, or other resources they can use? Make sure they have access to the tools they need to succeed.

此外，寻找拓展机会：有没有什么项目或职责能帮这个人练习他需要成长的技能？有没有书、课程或其他资源可供使用？确保他们能拿到成功所需的工具。

— PDF p.235 —

Finally, have a common way to track their progress. This will help with reflection and adjustment. Use your one-on-ones to check in on progress. Celebrate wins, talk about blockers, and be willing to adapt the plan as things evolve. The key is to make it a living document, not something you agree on once and forget about.

最后，建立一种共同的方式来跟踪他们的进展。这有助于反思和调整。利用一对一面谈检查进展。庆祝小胜、讨论阻塞、并愿意随着情况演进而调整计划。关键是让它成为一份活的文档，而不是你们定一次就抛在脑后的东西。

This tracking method also serves another purpose: it becomes your record of the steps taken. Documenting what's been tried—feedback shared, support offered, goals set, and check-ins held—ensures there's a complete picture of the situation. This helps the business make informed decisions if things escalate and reduces the risk of legal or procedural issues later on.

这种跟踪方式还有另一个用途：它成为你所采取步骤的记录。把试过的东西记录下来——分享过的反馈、提供过的支持、设定的目标、开过的同步会——确保对局面有一幅完整的图景。这有助于在情况升级时让公司做出明智决策，并降低日后出现法律或流程问题的风险。

You can find a much more detailed breakdown of each of these steps in the section “Developing a Personal Growth Plan” on page 38. That section is written for tech leads building their own growth path, but the same ideas apply perfectly when helping someone else grow too.

关于每一步更详细的拆解，见第 38 页“制定个人成长计划”一节。那一节是写给规划自己成长路径的技术负责人的，但同样的思路在帮别人成长时完全适用。

As you support their growth, keep your manager or HR partner in the loop. In some cases, the EM may want to co-own the plan or track progress directly. They'll also help decide what happens if things don't improve. That next step might involve moving toward a more formal process, such as a performance improvement plan (PIP), to ensure fairness, alignment, and compliance with company policies. The PIP provides one last structured opportunity for improvement with clearly defined goals, timelines, and outcomes.

在支持他们成长的过程中，让你的经理或 HR 伙伴知情。在某些情况下，工程经理可能想共同拥有这份计划、或直接跟踪进展。他们也会帮着决定：如果情况没有改善，下一步怎么办。下一步可能涉及走向更正式的流程，比如绩效改进计划（PIP），以确保公平、对齐、并符合公司政策。PIP 提供了最后一次结构化的改进机会，带有清晰界定的目标、时间线和结果。

Eventually, it may become clear that it's time to pull the plug and let someone go. This is one of the hardest processes you might face as a tech lead, but sometimes it's the only path left. Keeping someone in a role they're not suited for, despite support and second chances, not only continues to affect the rest of the team, but it can also hold the individual back from finding an environment where they could thrive. Letting someone go should always be done with compassion, transparency, and support, but avoiding it when it's clearly needed only prolongs the harm to everyone involved.

最终，可能会清楚地表明：是时候踩下刹车、让某个人离开了。这是你作为技术负责人可能面对的最难的流程之一，但有时它是唯一剩下的路。尽管给了支持和第二次机会，仍把一个人留在他并不适合的岗位上，不仅持续影响团队其他人，也会阻碍他去寻找一个能让他茁壮成长的环境。让一个人离开，始终应带着同理心、透明和支持去做；但在明确需要时回避它，只会延长对所有相关者的伤害。

Dealing with underperformance is never easy, but it's part of the job. When handled with care, honesty, and the right support, it can lead to real progress and prevent long-term damage to the team.

应对绩效不佳从来都不容易，但它是工作的一部分。当带着用心、诚实和恰当的支持去处理时，它可以带来真正的进步，并防止对团队的长期伤害。

— PDF p.236 —

Key Takeaway要点总结

Building and scaling a tech team is one of the most rewarding, and challenging, parts of being a tech lead. From recruiting and onboarding to running performance reviews and building team culture, you're responsible for shaping how your team grows, collaborates, and succeeds together.

组建和扩展一支技术团队，是作为技术负责人最有成就感、也最具挑战的部分之一。从招聘与入职，到开展绩效评估、建设团队文化，你负责塑造团队如何成长、如何协作、如何共同成功。

The work isn't always straightforward. You'll face ambiguity, tough conversations, and growing pains. But with the right mindset, clear systems, and a commitment to continuous improvement, you can create an environment where your team thrives.

这份工作并不总是一帆风顺。你会面对模糊、艰难的谈话和成长的阵痛。但只要有正确的心态、清晰的体系、以及对持续改进的承诺，你就能创造一个让团队茁壮成长的环境。

Whether you're preparing your first hiring plan or dealing with underperformance for the first time, I hope this chapter gave you the tools to take action with confidence, and reminded you that you don't have to get it perfect; just be intentional.

无论你是在准备第一份招聘计划、还是第一次应对绩效不佳，我都希望本章给了你带着信心去行动的工具，并提醒你：不必做到完美，只需刻意为之。
